Tests for {@link GroupedRandomAccessSource}, which stitches several underlying {@link RandomAccessSource}s together and exposes them as one contiguous block of data.

Each test groups three identical sources, every one holding the same {@value #SOURCE_LENGTH} bytes (the values 0..99). Because the sources are concatenated, the grouped source spans the global offset range [0, {@value #GROUPED_LENGTH}):

  • source 1 -> global offsets 0 .. 99
  • source 2 -> global offsets 100 .. 199
  • source 3 -> global offsets 200 .. 299
Number of bytes held by each individual underlying source.
Number of sources grouped together in every test.
Total length of the grouped source: every underlying source concatenated end to end.
Shared backing array containing the byte values 0, 1, 2, ... 99.
Builds a grouped source made of {@link #SOURCE_COUNT} sources, each backed by {@link #data}.
Single-byte reads should map a global offset to the right underlying source, and reads past the end of the grouped data should return -1.
The grouped length is the sum of all the underlying source lengths.
Global offsets are translated into (source, local offset) pairs.
last byte of source 1
first byte of source 2
second byte of source 2
back into source 1 again
last byte of source 3
Reading past the end of the grouped data signals end-of-data with -1.
Returns a byte array of {@code count} consecutive values starting at {@code start}, matching the values produced by {@link #setUp()} (i.e. byte i holds the value i).
Asserts that {@code len} bytes of {@code expected} (starting at {@code expectedOffset}) match {@code len} bytes of {@code actual} (starting at {@code actualOffset}).
Bulk reads should copy bytes across source boundaries, never read more than the available data even when more is requested, and honour a non-zero starting offset.
Reading the whole grouped range yields all GROUPED_LENGTH bytes: source 1, 2 then 3 back to back.
Requesting one byte more than exists still returns only the GROUPED_LENGTH available bytes.

Reading 100 bytes from global offset 150 spans the source 2 / source 3 boundary: offsets 150..199 are the second half of source 2 (local 50..99), offsets 200..249 are the first half of source 3 (local 0..49).
As reads move between sources, the grouped source must release the previously active source before putting the next one in use, so that exactly one underlying source is ever open.
Tracks the currently active source and how many sources are open, updated via the release/in-use callbacks below. Arrays are used so the anonymous subclass can mutate them.
Each pair of reads stays within one source, then the next pair jumps to a different source. After every jump the open count must remain 1, proving the old source was released first.
source 3
source 2
source 1
back to source 2
back to source 3
